title: Coordinated shim orchestration and staged symbol rollback for mixed CUDA/Triton stacks
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Resolve class of production flakes and OOMs caused by nondeterministic kernel symbol resolution across mixed CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS builds. Implement a coordinator that sequences shim activation, performs lightweight symbol validation, and provides an automated staged rollback path when symbol mismatches or regressions are detected.
background: We continue to see intermittent startup failures and runtime mis-dispatches on heterogeneous fleets where nodes have different CUTLASS/triton binary sets. Existing fixes (lazy loader, probe cache) reduced noise but don't provide an operationally safe rollback for live kernel bundle updates. Ops teams currently perform manual intervention (draining + swap) which is time consuming and error prone.
proposal:
1) Introduce a lightweight coordinator daemon (shim-orchestrator) that runs at node boot and during bundle activations.
2) Coordinator will validate symbol layout using an on-disk manifest and a fast symbol probe binary (no full model load).
3) If validation fails or telemetry shows regression during canary window, automatically switch to previously known-good symbol set via atomic bundle swap + pre-configured fallback policy.
4) Add opt-in feature flag to enable canary wave (percent of capacity) and a safety timeout that triggers rollback.
5) Emit structured telemetry for every activation to Console and a dedicated rollout dashboard.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Coordinator daemon deployed to canary fleet (5% of nodes) without user-visible impact.
2) Probe binary detects symbol layout mismatches within 2s on cold-start and reports to rollout dashboard.
3) Automated rollback triggers within configured timeout in 100% of failure-injection tests.
4) No measurable increase in cold-start latency beyond 10% in P50.
4) Documentation and runbook updated and SRE runbook validated in staging.
tasks:
- Design shim-orchestrator API and on-disk manifest schema (Aisha)
- Implement probe binary and unit tests (Rafael)
- Implement coordinator state machine + rollout policy engine (Rafael)
- Integrate with signed-kernel-bundle verification flow (Security)
- Add feature-flag + canary rollout infra to infra-deployer (Infra team)
- Create rollout dashboard in Console and tracing hooks (Observability)
- Create chaos tests that simulate symbol mismatch and measure rollback behavior (QA)
- Document runbook and post-rollout audit steps (SRE)
risks:
- False positives from probe causing unnecessary rollbacks (mitigate by conservative canary and multi-sample validation).
- Edge cases where symbol aliasing masks ABI incompatibility; mitigation: expand probe to run a small representative kernel invocation in staging.
- Security: coordinator must validate bundle signatures to avoid swapping to untrusted artifacts.
- Complexity: added state machine increases upgrade surface; limit initial rollout to non-critical pools.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for probe and manifest parsing.
- Integration tests: simulate mixed CUTLASS/CUDA versions and assert coordinator detects mismatch.
- Chaos test: inject corrupted symbol table and ensure rollback triggers and system recovers.
- Performance test: measure cold-start latency and P50/P95 on canary nodes before/after enabling coordinator.
- End-to-end canary rollout in staging with telemetry observed for 48 hours.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: deploy coordinator to 5% canary pool (non-critical region) with feature-flag off for automatic rollback. Monitor for 72h.
Phase 2: enable canary auto-rollback for that pool; run 1 week of increased telemetry.
Phase 3: expand to 25% with scheduled maintenance windows.
Phase 4: full rollout after sign-off and post-deployment audit.
